❯ Without using any tools, write a 1500-word essay on
  the history of the computer terminal, from teletypes
  to modern emulators.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  ⏸ plan mode on (shift+tab to cycle)
  The Persistence of the Terminal: From Teletypes to
  Modern Emulators

  The terminal is one of the oldest parts of computing
  still in daily use. A developer who opens a terminal
  window today is working inside a set of conventions
  older than the microprocessor: carriage returns, line
  feeds, control characters and escape sequences. Each
  was built to solve a problem with hardware, and each
  outlived the hardware it was built for. The history of
  the terminal is a history of compatibility: each
  generation imitated the one before it so faithfully
  that the imitation became the standard.

  Printing Telegraphs and the Teletype
